evidence: SettleClaim.settle loads the claim with this.claims.byId(claimId) and saves it with this.claims.save(claim), both through a port, so it coordinates the use case without doing persistence itself.
SettleClaim.settle gets coverage terms with this.coverage.termsFor(...) through the application port CoverageSource, with no transport or ACL logic in this file.
The business rules are handed to the domain: claim.decline() and claim.settle(new Money(terms.limitCents), new Money(terms.deductibleCents)) compute the paid amount inside the aggregate.
The not-found check throws DomainError('not-found', ...) without any HTTP status mapping, so no presentation concerns leak into this file.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: SettleClaim works as an application-layer use case. It loads the aggregate through the ClaimRepository port and fetches coverage terms through the CoverageSource application port. It then hands the business decisions to the aggregate (claim.decline(), claim.settle(limit, deductible)), saves the result through the port and returns a primitive. It holds no persistence code, transport or HTTP handling, or framework logic. It doesn't compute payouts itself: limit and deductible are applied inside the domain's settle method. Choosing to decline when no coverage terms are found is a branch in the use-case flow, and the decline itself still happens in the domain. Wrapping raw cents in Money value objects is ordinary port-to-domain mapping.
